お菓子|おかし.notes: Common N5 food word; 菓 is a higher-level kanji and must stay labeled on the N5 card.

exampleSentence.japanese: お菓子を少し食べます。
exampleSentence.reading: おかしをすこしたべます。
exampleSentence.english: I eat a few sweets.

exampleSentence.japanese: お金がありません。
exampleSentence.reading: おかねがありません。
exampleSentence.english: I do not have money.

お金|おかね.notes: Core money word; the polite お keeps this distinct from 金 as metal or gold.

exampleSentence.japanese: お父さんは会社から帰りました。
exampleSentence.reading: おとうさんはかいしゃからかえりました。
exampleSentence.english: My father came home from work.

お父さん|おとうさん.notes: Polite or familiar family term for father in beginner conversation; keeps 父 -> とう visible.

exampleSentence.japanese: お母さんは台所で料理しています。
exampleSentence.reading: おかあさんはだいどころでりょうりしています。
exampleSentence.english: My mother is cooking in the kitchen.

お母さん|おかあさん.notes: Polite or familiar family term for mother in beginner conversation; keeps 母 -> かあ visible.

椅子|いす.notes: Core classroom/household noun for chair; 椅 is outside the JLPT kanji contract and the N5 reading support remains 子 -> す.

exampleSentence.japanese: 椅子に座ってください。
exampleSentence.reading: いすにすわってください。
exampleSentence.english: Please sit in the chair.

一|いち.notes: Common standalone number form for counting sequences and number ranges.

exampleSentence.japanese: 一から十まで言います。
exampleSentence.reading: いちからじゅうまでいいます。
exampleSentence.english: I say one through ten.

exampleSentence.japanese: りんごを一つください。
exampleSentence.reading: りんごをひとつください。
exampleSentence.english: Please give me one apple.

一つ|ひとつ.notes: Core native counter form for one thing; useful for beginner requests.

exampleSentence.japanese: 一時に会いましょう。
exampleSentence.reading: いちじにあいましょう。
exampleSentence.english: Let's meet at one o'clock.

一時|いちじ.notes: Core time expression for one o'clock; reviewed for the clock-time sense.

一時半|いちじはん.notes: Learn this as a common time expression: 一時半 means half past one / 1:30.

exampleSentence.japanese: 一時半に会いましょう。
exampleSentence.reading: いちじはんにあいましょう。
exampleSentence.english: Let's meet at half past one.

一緒|いっしょ.notes: Core beginner word for doing something together; 緒 is higher-level kanji support and generated pitch remains visibly labeled.

exampleSentence.japanese: 友だちと一緒に行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: ともだちといっしょにいきます。
exampleSentence.english: I go together with my friend.

一人|ひとり.notes: Irregular counter reading. Learn this as a whole word: 一人 is the core people-count word for one person or alone.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今日は一人で帰ります。
exampleSentence.reading: きょうはひとりでかえります。
exampleSentence.english: Today I will go home alone.

一日|いちにち.notes: Core duration word for one day or all day; distinguish from 一日|ついたち, the first day of the month.

exampleSentence.japanese: 一日だけ休みます。
exampleSentence.reading: いちにちだけやすみます。
exampleSentence.english: I will rest for one day.

一日|ついたち.meaning: the first day of the month
一日|ついたち.notes: Common date word with a whole-word reading; do not split it into false per-kanji readings.

exampleSentence.japanese: 来月の一日に学校へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: らいげつのついたちにがっこうへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: I go to school on the first of next month.

exampleSentence.japanese: この時計は一万円です。
exampleSentence.reading: このとけいはいちまんえんです。
exampleSentence.english: This watch costs 10,000 yen.

一万円|いちまんえん.notes: Core price expression for 10,000 yen; useful for shopping examples.

exampleSentence.japanese: 右に曲がります。
exampleSentence.reading: みぎにまがります。
exampleSentence.english: I turn right.

右|みぎ.notes: Core direction word for right; this word-card reading is みぎ, separate from on-readings in compounds.

exampleSentence.japanese: 右手で書いています。
exampleSentence.reading: みぎてでかいています。
exampleSentence.english: I am writing with my right hand.

右手|みぎて.notes: Core body/direction word for right hand; 手 is higher-level kanji support and the N5 focus remains 右 -> みぎ.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今日は雨です。
exampleSentence.reading: きょうはあめです。
exampleSentence.english: It is raining today.

雨|あめ.notes: Core weather word for rain; this word-card reading is あめ and uses a simple weather example.

exampleSentence.japanese: 英語を勉強します。
exampleSentence.reading: えいごをべんきょうします。
exampleSentence.english: I study English.

英語|えいご.notes: Core language word for English; 英 is higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 語 -> ご.

exampleSentence.japanese: 駅前で友だちを待ちます。
exampleSentence.reading: えきまえでともだちをまちます。
exampleSentence.english: I wait for my friend in front of the station.

駅前|えきまえ.notes: Common station/place word for in front of the station; 駅 is higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 前 -> まえ.

円高|えんだか.notes: Dictionary-backed money/news support word for 高 -> だか; useful for yen exchange contexts, but not a core beginner conversation word.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今は円高です。
exampleSentence.reading: いまはえんだかです。
exampleSentence.english: The yen is strong now.

音読|おんどく.notes: Common classroom and study word; retained because it gives real 読 -> どく usage in a useful learning context, with 音 visibly labeled as JLPT N4 kanji.

exampleSentence.japanese: 教室で音読をしました。
exampleSentence.reading: きょうしつでおんどくをしました。
exampleSentence.english: We read aloud in the classroom.

exampleSentence.japanese: いすの下に猫がいます。
exampleSentence.reading: いすのしたにねこがいます。
exampleSentence.english: There is a cat under the chair.

下|した.notes: Core location word for under/below; this word-card reading is した.

exampleSentence.japanese: ねだんが下がりました。
exampleSentence.reading: ねだんがさがりました。
exampleSentence.english: The price went down.

下がる|さがる.notes: Common intransitive verb for going down or falling; useful for prices and levels.

下さい|ください.notes: Useful polite request form connected to the ください reading; usually written in kana as ください, so this card is for recognizing the kanji spelling 下さい when it appears.

exampleSentence.japanese: 水を下さい。
exampleSentence.reading: みずをください。
exampleSentence.english: Please give me water.

exampleSentence.japanese: 階段を下ります。
exampleSentence.reading: かいだんをおります。
exampleSentence.english: I go down the stairs.

下りる|おりる.notes: Common motion verb for going down or getting off; keeps 下りる distinct from 下がる and 下る.

exampleSentence.japanese: 私は歌が下手です。
exampleSentence.reading: わたしはうたがへたです。
exampleSentence.english: I am bad at singing.

下手|へた.notes: Very common bad-at adjective and 上手 counterpart; useful support for 手 -> た with 手 visibly labeled as higher-level.

下町|したまち.notes: Common Japan place/culture word; retained because it gives useful 下 -> した usage in a real town/neighborhood context, with 町 visibly labeled as JLPT N4 kanji.

exampleSentence.japanese: 下町をゆっくり歩きました。
exampleSentence.reading: したまちをゆっくりあるきました。
exampleSentence.english: I took a slow walk through the old downtown area.

exampleSentence.japanese: 何を飲みますか。
exampleSentence.reading: なにをのみますか。
exampleSentence.english: What will you drink?

何|なに.notes: Core question word for what; this card teaches 何 as なに, separate from なん contexts.

何ですか|なんですか.notes: Fixed polite beginner question expression built from 何 plus ですか; useful for classroom and basic conversation, not arbitrary phrase approval.

exampleSentence.japanese: これは何ですか。
exampleSentence.reading: これはなんですか。
exampleSentence.english: What is this?

何時|なんじ.notes: Core question word for asking what time; useful with 何時ですか.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今、何時ですか。
exampleSentence.reading: いま、なんじですか。
exampleSentence.english: What time is it now?

exampleSentence.japanese: 火を消してください。
exampleSentence.reading: ひをけしてください。
exampleSentence.english: Please put out the fire.

火|ひ.notes: Core noun for fire; this word-card reading is ひ, separate from weekday and compound readings.

火照る|ほてる.notes: Natural body-state verb; retained because it gives real 火 -> ほ usage, not coverage padding, with 照 visibly labeled as JLPT N2 kanji.

exampleSentence.japanese: 走った後で顔が火照っています。
exampleSentence.reading: はしったあとでかおがほてっています。
exampleSentence.english: My face feels hot after running.

exampleSentence.japanese: 火曜日は日本語のクラスがあります。
exampleSentence.reading: かようびはにほんごのクラスがあります。
exampleSentence.english: I have Japanese class on Tuesday.

火曜日|かようび.notes: Core weekday word for Tuesday; 曜 is higher-level support and the N5 focus covers 火 -> か and 日 -> び.

exampleSentence.japanese: 友だちと会話をします。
exampleSentence.reading: ともだちとかいわをします。
exampleSentence.english: I have a conversation with my friend.

会話|かいわ.notes: Common communication word for conversation; 会 is higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 話 -> わ.

外|そと.notes: Core location word for outside; this word-card reading is そと, separate from kanji-deck reading review.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今日は外で昼ご飯を食べます。
exampleSentence.reading: きょうはそとでひるごはんをたべます。
exampleSentence.english: Today I eat lunch outside.

外す|はずす.notes: Common support word for 外 -> はずす. Use it for removing things like glasses, buttons, or parts; shoes are normally 脱ぐ.

exampleSentence.japanese: メガネを外します。
exampleSentence.reading: メガネをはずします。
exampleSentence.english: I take off my glasses.

外科|げか.notes: Common medical-department word; support-only for 外 -> げ with 科 visibly labeled as higher-level.

exampleSentence.japanese: 父は外科へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: ちちはげかへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: My father goes to the surgical department.

exampleSentence.japanese: 外国へ行きたいです。
exampleSentence.reading: がいこくへいきたいです。
exampleSentence.english: I want to go abroad.

外国|がいこく.notes: Core word for a foreign country or abroad; useful for travel and comparison contexts.

exampleSentence.japanese: 外国人の友だちがいます。
exampleSentence.reading: がいこくじんのともだちがいます。
exampleSentence.english: I have a foreign friend.

外国人|がいこくじん.notes: Common word for a foreign person or foreign national; use with context and avoid reducing people to labels.

exampleSentence.japanese: 八時に学校へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: はちじにがっこうへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: I go to school at eight o'clock.

学校|がっこう.notes: Core school word; useful for everyday education and schedule contexts.

exampleSentence.japanese: あの人は学生です。
exampleSentence.reading: あのひとはがくせいです。
exampleSentence.english: That person is a student.

学生|がくせい.notes: Core school/person word for student; useful for introductions and classroom contexts.

exampleSentence.japanese: 休みの間、本を読みます。
exampleSentence.reading: やすみのあいだ、ほんをよみます。
exampleSentence.english: I read books during the break.

間|あいだ.notes: Core word for an interval, space between things, or while span; this card teaches 間 as あいだ.

関西|かんさい.notes: Common Japan geography word; retained because it gives useful 西 -> さい usage for the Kansai region, with 関 visibly labeled as JLPT N3 kanji.

exampleSentence.japanese: 春に関西へ旅行します。
exampleSentence.reading: はるにかんさいへりょこうします。
exampleSentence.english: I will travel to Kansai in the spring.

休み|やすみ.notes: Common noun for a break, day off, or holiday; distinct from the verb 休む.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今日は学校が休みです。
exampleSentence.reading: きょうはがっこうがやすみです。
exampleSentence.english: School is off today.

exampleSentence.japanese: 休み時間に友だちと話します。
exampleSentence.reading: やすみじかんにともだちとはなします。
exampleSentence.english: I talk with my friend during break time.

休み時間|やすみじかん.notes: Common school word; retained because it teaches useful 休み, 時, and 間 readings in a practical break-time context.

休む|やすむ.notes: Core verb for resting or taking time off; useful before related noun forms like 休み.

exampleSentence.japanese: 日曜日は家で休みます。
exampleSentence.reading: にちようびはいえでやすみます。
exampleSentence.english: I rest at home on Sunday.

exampleSentence.japanese: 休日は家でゆっくり休みます。
exampleSentence.reading: きゅうじつはいえでゆっくりやすみます。
exampleSentence.english: I rest at home on my day off.

休日|きゅうじつ.notes: Common schedule word for a holiday or day off; useful support for 休 -> きゅう and 日 -> じつ.

exampleSentence.japanese: 去年、日本へ行きました。
exampleSentence.reading: きょねん、にほんへいきました。
exampleSentence.english: I went to Japan last year.

去年|きょねん.notes: Core beginner time word for last year; 去 is higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 年 -> ねん.

金具|かなぐ.notes: Common concrete hardware word for metal fittings; useful support for 金 -> かな with 具 visibly labeled as higher-level.

exampleSentence.japanese: かばんの金具は小さいです。
exampleSentence.reading: かばんのかなぐはちいさいです。
exampleSentence.english: The metal fitting on the bag is small.

exampleSentence.japanese: 金曜日に友だちと会います。
exampleSentence.reading: きんようびにともだちとあいます。
exampleSentence.english: I will meet my friend on Friday.

金曜日|きんようび.notes: Core weekday word for Friday; 曜 is higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 金 -> きん.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今日、銀行へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: きょう、ぎんこうへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: Today I am going to the bank.

銀行|ぎんこう.notes: Core beginner errand word for bank; 銀 is higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 行 -> こう.

九|きゅう.notes: Core standalone number form for nine; useful for number sequences and counting contexts.

exampleSentence.japanese: 数字を一から九まで言います。
exampleSentence.reading: すうじをいちからきゅうまでいいます。
exampleSentence.english: I say the numbers from one to nine.

exampleSentence.japanese: 皿が九つあります。
exampleSentence.reading: さらがここのつあります。
exampleSentence.english: There are nine plates.

九つ|ここのつ.notes: Core counter form for nine things; this card teaches the ここのつ reading for general counting.

exampleSentence.japanese: 九時に学校へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: くじにがっこうへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: I go to school at nine o'clock.

九時|くじ.notes: Core time expression for nine o'clock; useful for schedules and school routines.

九日|ここのか.notes: Common date and duration word with a whole-word reading; do not split it into false per-kanji readings.

exampleSentence.japanese: 九日に学校へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: ここのかにがっこうへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: I go to school on the ninth.

靴下|くつした.notes: Common N5 clothing word; 靴 is a higher-level kanji and must stay labeled on the N5 card.

exampleSentence.japanese: 靴下をはきます。
exampleSentence.reading: くつしたをはきます。
exampleSentence.english: I put on socks.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今夜は月がきれいです。
exampleSentence.reading: こんやはつきがきれいです。
exampleSentence.english: The moon is beautiful tonight.

月|つき.notes: Common standalone word for the moon; this word-card reading つき is separate from month names like 一月.

exampleSentence.japanese: 月曜日に学校へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: げつようびにがっこうへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: I go to school on Monday.

月曜日|げつようび.notes: Core weekday word for Monday; 曜 is higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 月 -> げつ.

exampleSentence.japanese: 山がよく見えます。
exampleSentence.reading: やまがよくみえます。
exampleSentence.english: I can see the mountain clearly.

見える|みえる.notes: Core verb for being visible or being able to see; contrast with 見る for intentional looking.

exampleSentence.japanese: 先生に宿題を見せます。
exampleSentence.reading: せんせいにしゅくだいをみせます。
exampleSentence.english: I show my homework to the teacher.

見せる|みせる.notes: Common transitive verb for showing something; keeps 見せる distinct from 見る.

exampleSentence.japanese: 家で映画を見る。
exampleSentence.reading: いえでえいがをみる。
exampleSentence.english: I watch a movie at home.

見る|みる.notes: Common verb for seeing or watching; keeps 見る distinct from 見せる.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今日は元気です。
exampleSentence.reading: きょうはげんきです。
exampleSentence.english: I am well today.

元気|げんき.notes: Core beginner word for being well or energetic; 元 is higher-level support that covers the N4 元 -> げん reading, while the N5 placement remains anchored by 気 -> き.

五|ご.notes: Core standalone number form for five; useful for number sequences and counting contexts.

exampleSentence.japanese: 数字を五から八まで言います。
exampleSentence.reading: すうじをごからはちまでいいます。
exampleSentence.english: I say the numbers from five to eight.

exampleSentence.japanese: クッキーを五つ食べました。
exampleSentence.reading: くっきーをいつつたべました。
exampleSentence.english: I ate five cookies.

五つ|いつつ.notes: Core counter form for five things; this card teaches the いつつ reading for general counting.

五月|ごがつ.notes: Core month word for May; reinforces 五 -> ご and 月 -> がつ in a common calendar word.

exampleSentence.japanese: 五月はあたたかい日が多いです。
exampleSentence.reading: ごがつはあたたかいひがおおいです。
exampleSentence.english: There are many warm days in May.

exampleSentence.japanese: 五時に店が閉まります。
exampleSentence.reading: ごじにみせがしまります。
exampleSentence.english: The shop closes at five o'clock.

五時|ごじ.notes: Core time expression for five o'clock; useful for schedules and closing times.

五日|いつか.notes: Common date and duration word with a whole-word reading; do not split it into false per-kanji readings.

exampleSentence.japanese: 来月の五日に会います。
exampleSentence.reading: らいげつのいつかにあいます。
exampleSentence.english: I will meet on the fifth of next month.

exampleSentence.japanese: 駅まで五分かかります。
exampleSentence.reading: えきまでごふんかかります。
exampleSentence.english: It takes five minutes to get to the station.

五分|ごふん.notes: Core duration word for five minutes; useful for travel-time and schedule examples.

exampleSentence.japanese: 午後は図書館で本を読みます。
exampleSentence.reading: ごごはとしょかんでほんをよみます。
exampleSentence.english: In the afternoon I read books at the library.

午後|ごご.notes: Core time-of-day word for afternoon or p.m.; complements 午前.

exampleSentence.japanese: 午前九時に学校へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: ごぜんくじにがっこうへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: I go to school at 9 a.m.

午前|ごぜん.notes: Core time-of-day word for morning or a.m.; complements 午後.

午年|うまどし.notes: Dictionary-backed zodiac-year support word for 午 -> うま; kept for cultural and reading coverage, with generated pitch visibly labeled.

exampleSentence.japanese: 父は午年です。
exampleSentence.reading: ちちはうまどしです。
exampleSentence.english: My father was born in the Year of the Horse.

後|あと.notes: Common time/reference noun for after or later; complements 後で and 後ろ without replacing them.

exampleSentence.japanese: ご飯の後で水を飲みます。
exampleSentence.reading: ごはんのあとでみずをのみます。
exampleSentence.english: I drink water after the meal.

後で|あとで.notes: Common time expression meaning later; often written in kana as あとで, with 後 providing あと reading coverage.

exampleSentence.japanese: 後で電話します。
exampleSentence.reading: あとででんわします。
exampleSentence.english: I will call later.

後ほど|のちほど.notes: Polite later/afterward support word for 後 -> のち; useful in messages and service contexts but support-only for N5.

exampleSentence.japanese: 後ほど電話します。
exampleSentence.reading: のちほどでんわします。
exampleSentence.english: I will call later.

exampleSentence.japanese: 家の後ろに小さい公園があります。
exampleSentence.reading: いえのうしろにちいさいこうえんがあります。
exampleSentence.english: There is a small park behind the house.

後ろ|うしろ.notes: Common location noun for behind or back; complements 後 and 後で without replacing them.

後半|こうはん.notes: Dictionary-backed support word for second or latter half; kept for useful book/time contexts and 後 -> こう coverage.

exampleSentence.japanese: 本の後半を読みます。
exampleSentence.reading: ほんのこうはんをよみます。
exampleSentence.english: I read the second half of the book.

語らう|かたらう.notes: Dictionary-backed support verb for 語 -> かたらう; kept support-only and not as a core substitute for beginner 話す or 話.

exampleSentence.japanese: 友だちと楽しく語らう。
exampleSentence.reading: ともだちとたのしくかたらう。
exampleSentence.english: I enjoy talking together with my friend.

行きます|いきます.notes: Polite form of 行く; useful for hearing いきます directly, but reviewed as a conjugated support form rather than a separate JMdict headword.

exampleSentence.japanese: 毎朝七時に学校へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: まいあさしちじにがっこうへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: I go to school at seven every morning.

行き先|ゆきさき.notes: Common destination word. Also read いきさき; this card uses ゆきさき for the 行 -> ゆき travel/signage reading.

exampleSentence.japanese: 行き先を書いてください。
exampleSentence.reading: ゆきさきをかいてください。
exampleSentence.english: Please write your destination.

exampleSentence.japanese: 学校へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: がっこうへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: I go to school.

行く|いく.notes: Core verb for going; the example uses a simple school destination context.

行事|ぎょうじ.notes: Common school/event word; useful support for 行 -> ぎょう with 事 visibly labeled as higher-level.

exampleSentence.japanese: 学校の行事で公園へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: がっこうのぎょうじでこうえんへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: We go to the park for a school event.

exampleSentence.japanese: このりんごは高いです。
exampleSentence.reading: このりんごはたかいです。
exampleSentence.english: This apple is expensive.

高い|たかい.notes: Core adjective for height or price; the example uses the beginner-useful expensive sense.

exampleSentence.japanese: 高校で勉強します。
exampleSentence.reading: こうこうでべんきょうします。
exampleSentence.english: I study at a high school.

高校|こうこう.notes: Core school word for high school; useful for education and student contexts.

exampleSentence.japanese: 日本はきれいな国です。
exampleSentence.reading: にほんはきれいなくにです。
exampleSentence.english: Japan is a beautiful country.

国|くに.notes: Core noun for country; this word-card reading is くに, separate from compound readings like 国語.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今、家に帰ります。
exampleSentence.reading: いま、いえにかえります。
exampleSentence.english: I am going home now.

今|いま.notes: Core time word for now; this word-card reading is いま, separate from compound readings like 今日.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今月、日本へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: こんげつ、にほんへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: This month I will go to Japan.

今月|こんげつ.notes: Core time word for this month; useful for current plans.

今週|こんしゅう.notes: Core beginner time word for this week; 週 is higher-level kanji support and generated pitch remains visibly labeled.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今週、学校へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: こんしゅう、がっこうへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: I will go to school this week.

今朝|けさ.notes: Common N5 time word with a whole-word reading; 朝 is a higher-level kanji and the card must not be split into false per-kanji readings.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今朝、水を飲みました。
exampleSentence.reading: けさ、みずをのみました。
exampleSentence.english: I drank water this morning.

今日|きょう.notes: Irregular reading. Learn this as a whole word: 今日 is the core time word for today.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今日は学校へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: きょうはがっこうへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: Today I am going to school.

今年|ことし.notes: Core time word for this year; useful for plans and annual events. Learn 今年 as the whole-word reading ことし.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今年は日本へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: ことしはにほんへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: This year I will go to Japan.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今晩、家で本を読みます。
exampleSentence.reading: こんばん、いえでほんをよみます。
exampleSentence.english: Tonight, I read a book at home.

今晩|こんばん.notes: Core time word for tonight; 晩 is higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 今 -> こん.

exampleSentence.japanese: 左に郵便局があります。
exampleSentence.reading: ひだりにゆうびんきょくがあります。
exampleSentence.english: There is a post office on the left.

左|ひだり.notes: Core direction word for left; this word-card reading is ひだり, separate from compound readings.

左右|さゆう.notes: Reading-coverage support word for the common 左 -> さ and 右 -> ゆう pattern.

exampleSentence.japanese: 左右を見てから道を渡ってください。
exampleSentence.reading: さゆうをみてからみちをわたってください。
exampleSentence.english: Please look left and right before crossing the road.

exampleSentence.japanese: 左手でコップを持ちます。
exampleSentence.reading: ひだりてでこっぷをもちます。
exampleSentence.english: I hold the cup with my left hand.

左手|ひだりて.notes: Core body/direction word for left hand; 手 is higher-level kanji support and the N5 focus remains 左 -> ひだり.

左折|させつ.notes: Common navigation and signage word for a left turn; useful support for 左 -> さ, while ひだり remains the everyday standalone left.

exampleSentence.japanese: ここで左折します。
exampleSentence.reading: ここでさせつします。
exampleSentence.english: I turn left here.

昨日|きのう.notes: Common N5 time word with a whole-word reading; 昨 is a higher-level kanji and the card must not be split into false per-kanji readings.

exampleSentence.japanese: 昨日、映画を見ました。
exampleSentence.reading: きのう、えいがをみました。
exampleSentence.english: I watched a movie yesterday.

三|さん.notes: Core standalone number form for three; useful for number sequences and counting contexts.

exampleSentence.japanese: 数字を三から六まで言います。
exampleSentence.reading: すうじをさんからろくまでいいます。
exampleSentence.english: I say the numbers from three to six.

exampleSentence.japanese: りんごを三つ買いました。
exampleSentence.reading: りんごをみっつかいました。
exampleSentence.english: I bought three apples.

三つ|みっつ.notes: Common counter form for three things; learn みっつ as a whole counter word.

exampleSentence.japanese: 三時に図書館で会いましょう。
exampleSentence.reading: さんじにとしょかんであいましょう。
exampleSentence.english: Let's meet at the library at three o'clock.

三時|さんじ.notes: Core time expression for three o'clock; useful for schedules and meeting times.

exampleSentence.japanese: 三人で映画を見ます。
exampleSentence.reading: さんにんでえいがをみます。
exampleSentence.english: The three of us will watch a movie.

三人|さんにん.notes: Core people-count word for three people; useful for group-size examples.

三日|みっか.notes: Common date and duration word with a whole-word reading; do not split it into false per-kanji readings.

exampleSentence.japanese: 三日に会います。
exampleSentence.reading: みっかにあいます。
exampleSentence.english: I will meet on the third.

三百|さんびゃく.notes: Common number word for three hundred; kept for 百 -> びゃく number-sound change without unrelated dictionary senses.

exampleSentence.japanese: この本は三百円です。
exampleSentence.reading: このほんはさんびゃくえんです。
exampleSentence.english: This book costs three hundred yen.

exampleSentence.japanese: 山が見えます。
exampleSentence.reading: やまがみえます。
exampleSentence.english: I can see a mountain.

山|やま.notes: Core nature noun for mountain; this word-card reading is やま.

四|よん.notes: Common standalone number form for counting sequences and number ranges.

exampleSentence.japanese: 数字を四から七まで言います。
exampleSentence.reading: すうじをよんからななまでいいます。
exampleSentence.english: I say the numbers from four to seven.

exampleSentence.japanese: コップが四つあります。
exampleSentence.reading: こっぷがよっつあります。
exampleSentence.english: There are four cups.

四つ|よっつ.notes: Core native counter form for four things; useful for everyday quantities.

四月|しがつ.notes: Core month word for April; reinforces 四 -> し and 月 -> がつ in a common calendar word.

exampleSentence.japanese: 四月に学校が始まります。
exampleSentence.reading: しがつにがっこうがはじまります。
exampleSentence.english: School starts in April.

exampleSentence.japanese: 四時に家へ帰ります。
exampleSentence.reading: よじにいえへかえります。
exampleSentence.english: I go home at four o'clock.

四時|よじ.notes: Core time expression for four o'clock; useful for schedules and returning home.

四日|よっか.notes: Common date and duration word with a whole-word reading; do not split it into false per-kanji readings.

exampleSentence.japanese: 四日に電話します。
exampleSentence.reading: よっかにでんわします。
exampleSentence.english: I will call on the fourth.

exampleSentence.japanese: 子どもが公園で遊んでいます。
exampleSentence.reading: こどもがこうえんであそんでいます。
exampleSentence.english: A child is playing in the park.

子ども|こども.notes: Core word for child; this mixed 子ども form is learner-friendly and equivalent to 子供.

exampleSentence.japanese: 小さい子犬がいます。
exampleSentence.reading: ちいさいこいぬがいます。
exampleSentence.english: There is a small puppy.

子犬|こいぬ.notes: Common concrete word for puppy; 犬 is higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 子 -> こ.

exampleSentence.japanese: 子猫がいます。
exampleSentence.reading: こねこがいます。
exampleSentence.english: There is a kitten.

子猫|こねこ.notes: Common word for kitten; 猫 is a higher-level support kanji and must stay visibly labeled.

子年|ねどし.notes: Zodiac-year support word for 子 -> ね; useful for recognizing birth-year contexts, not everyday 子 -> こ, and generated pitch remains visibly labeled.

exampleSentence.japanese: 私は子年です。
exampleSentence.reading: わたしはねどしです。
exampleSentence.english: I was born in the Year of the Rat.

exampleSentence.japanese: 時々公園で友だちに会います。
exampleSentence.reading: ときどきこうえんでともだちにあいます。
exampleSentence.english: I sometimes meet my friend at the park.

時々|ときどき.notes: Core frequency adverb meaning sometimes; this card teaches 時々 as ときどき.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今日は勉強する時間があります。
exampleSentence.reading: きょうはべんきょうするじかんがあります。
exampleSentence.english: Today I have time to study.

時間|じかん.notes: Core word for time or hour; useful for schedules, study, and availability.

時計|とけい.notes: Common N5 object word; 計 is a higher-level kanji and must stay labeled on the N5 card.

exampleSentence.japanese: 時計を見ます。
exampleSentence.reading: とけいをみます。
exampleSentence.english: I look at the clock.

exampleSentence.japanese: 自転車で学校へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: じてんしゃでがっこうへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: I go to school by bicycle.

自転車|じてんしゃ.notes: Core bicycle word; 自 and 転 are higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 車 -> しゃ.

自分|じぶん.notes: Common N5 pronoun; 自 is a higher-level kanji and must stay labeled on the N5 card.

exampleSentence.japanese: 自分の名前を書きます。
exampleSentence.reading: じぶんのなまえをかきます。
exampleSentence.english: I write my own name.

exampleSentence.japanese: 新しい辞書を買いました。
exampleSentence.reading: あたらしいじしょをかいました。
exampleSentence.english: I bought a new dictionary.

辞書|じしょ.notes: Core school/tool word for dictionary; 辞 is higher-level kanji support and the N5 focus remains 書 -> しょ.

七|なな.notes: Common standalone number form for counting sequences and number ranges.

exampleSentence.japanese: 七から十まで言います。
exampleSentence.reading: ななからじゅうまでいいます。
exampleSentence.english: I say seven through ten.

exampleSentence.japanese: 質問が七つあります。
exampleSentence.reading: しつもんがななつあります。
exampleSentence.english: There are seven questions.

七つ|ななつ.notes: Core native counter form for seven things; useful for everyday quantities.

exampleSentence.japanese: 七時に朝ご飯を食べます。
exampleSentence.reading: しちじにあさごはんをたべます。
exampleSentence.english: I eat breakfast at seven o'clock.

七時|しちじ.notes: Core time expression for seven o'clock; useful for daily routines.

七日|なのか.notes: Common date and duration word; treat なのか as a fixed calendar reading, with 日 -> か as the date suffix.

exampleSentence.japanese: テストは七日にあります。
exampleSentence.reading: テストはなのかにあります。
exampleSentence.english: The test is on the seventh.

社長|しゃちょう.notes: Common workplace title; retained because it gives useful 長 -> ちょう usage with 社 visibly labeled as JLPT N4 kanji.

exampleSentence.japanese: 社長は朝早く会社に来ます。
exampleSentence.reading: しゃちょうはあさはやくかいしゃにきます。
exampleSentence.english: The company president comes to the office early in the morning.

exampleSentence.japanese: 白い車があります。
exampleSentence.reading: しろいくるまがあります。
exampleSentence.english: There is a white car.

車|くるま.notes: Core noun for car or vehicle; this word-card reading is くるま.

手間|てま.notes: Common time-and-effort word; retained because it gives useful 間 -> ま usage in the practical 手間がかかる pattern, with 手 visibly labeled as JLPT N4 kanji.

exampleSentence.japanese: 手間がかかる仕事です。
exampleSentence.reading: てまがかかるしごとです。
exampleSentence.english: It is a job that takes a lot of effort.

手本|てほん.notes: Common classroom/study word; retained because it is useful for copying a model or example, not merely to cover 本 -> ほん.

exampleSentence.japanese: 手本を見て書きます。
exampleSentence.reading: てほんをみてかきます。
exampleSentence.english: I look at the model and write.

十|じゅう.notes: Core standalone number form for ten; this card teaches じゅう for number and number-sequence use.

exampleSentence.japanese: 数字を一から十まで言います。
exampleSentence.reading: すうじをいちからじゅうまでいいます。
exampleSentence.english: I say the numbers from one to ten.

十回|じっかい.notes: Practical counter expression for ten times; useful support for 十 -> じっ with 回 visibly labeled as higher-level and generated pitch visibly labeled.

exampleSentence.japanese: この漢字を十回書いてください。
exampleSentence.reading: このかんじをじっかいかいてください。
exampleSentence.english: Please write this kanji ten times.

exampleSentence.japanese: 十時に寝ます。
exampleSentence.reading: じゅうじにねます。
exampleSentence.english: I go to bed at ten o'clock.

十時|じゅうじ.notes: Core time expression for ten o'clock; useful for daily routines.

十日|とおか.notes: Common date and duration word with a whole-word reading; do not split it into false per-kanji readings.

exampleSentence.japanese: テストは十日にあります。
exampleSentence.reading: てすとはとおかにあります。
exampleSentence.english: The test is on the tenth.

exampleSentence.japanese: 駅まで十分かかります。
exampleSentence.reading: えきまでじゅっぷんかかります。
exampleSentence.english: It takes ten minutes to get to the station.

十分|じゅっぷん.notes: Core duration word for ten minutes; reviewed as じゅっぷん, not 十分|じゅうぶん meaning enough.

出かける|でかける.notes: Common beginner verb for going out or leaving; useful everyday action word.

exampleSentence.japanese: 明日、友だちと出かけます。
exampleSentence.reading: あした、ともだちとでかけます。
exampleSentence.english: Tomorrow I will go out with a friend.

exampleSentence.japanese: かばんから本を出します。
exampleSentence.reading: かばんからほんをだします。
exampleSentence.english: I take a book out of my bag.

出す|だす.notes: Common transitive verb for taking or putting something out; keeps 出す distinct from 出る.

exampleSentence.japanese: 朝、家を出る。
exampleSentence.reading: あさ、いえをでる。
exampleSentence.english: I leave the house in the morning.

出る|でる.notes: Core verb for leaving or going out; the example keeps 出る visible in dictionary form for the でる reading.

exampleSentence.japanese: 出口で友だちを待ちます。
exampleSentence.reading: でぐちでともだちをまちます。
exampleSentence.english: I will wait for my friend at the exit.

出口|でぐち.notes: Core navigation word for exit; 口 is higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 出 -> で.

春雨|はるさめ.notes: Common food and seasonal word; retained because it gives real learner-facing 雨 -> さめ usage with 春 visibly labeled as higher-level.

exampleSentence.japanese: 春雨スープを食べます。
exampleSentence.reading: はるさめスープをたべます。
exampleSentence.english: I eat harusame soup.

exampleSentence.japanese: ノートに名前を書きます。
exampleSentence.reading: のーとになまえをかきます。
exampleSentence.english: I write my name in the notebook.

書く|かく.notes: Core verb for writing; the example keeps 書く in a practical name-writing context.

女|おんな.notes: Can sound blunt when used alone; 女の人 is the safer beginner phrase for a woman, and 女の子 means girl.

exampleSentence.japanese: 女の人が店に入ります。
exampleSentence.reading: おんなのひとがみせにはいります。
exampleSentence.english: A woman enters the shop.

exampleSentence.japanese: あの女の子は元気です。
exampleSentence.reading: あのおんなのこはげんきです。
exampleSentence.english: That girl is energetic.

女の子|おんなのこ.notes: Common beginner word for girl; fixed の expression that belongs as a word card, not arbitrary phrase padding.

女神|めがみ.notes: Common myth and story word; retained because it gives real 女 -> め usage while 神 is visibly labeled as JLPT N3 kanji.

exampleSentence.japanese: 物語に海の女神が出てきます。
exampleSentence.reading: ものがたりにうみのめがみがでてきます。
exampleSentence.english: A sea goddess appears in the story.

exampleSentence.japanese: この犬は小さいです。
exampleSentence.reading: このいぬはちいさいです。
exampleSentence.english: This dog is small.

小さい|ちいさい.notes: Core adjective for small; this word-card reading is ちいさい.

小雨|こさめ.notes: Dictionary-backed weather support word for light rain; useful for 雨 -> さめ coverage but support-only, not a core substitute for 雨.

exampleSentence.japanese: 朝から小雨が降っています。
exampleSentence.reading: あさからこさめがふっています。
exampleSentence.english: A light rain has been falling since morning.

exampleSentence.japanese: 弟は小学校へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: おとうとはしょうがっこうへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: My younger brother goes to elementary school.

小学校|しょうがっこう.notes: Core school word for elementary school; useful for education contexts.

小指|こゆび.notes: Common body-part word for little finger or pinky; useful support for 小 -> こ with 指 visibly labeled as higher-level.

exampleSentence.japanese: 小指が痛いです。
exampleSentence.reading: こゆびがいたいです。
exampleSentence.english: My little finger hurts.

小川|おがわ.notes: Dictionary-backed nature/place word for stream; useful for 小 -> お coverage but support-only for N5.

exampleSentence.japanese: 小川があります。
exampleSentence.reading: おがわがあります。
exampleSentence.english: There is a stream.

exampleSentence.japanese: 机の上に本があります。
exampleSentence.reading: つくえのうえにほんがあります。
exampleSentence.english: There is a book on the desk.

上|うえ.notes: Common location noun for up, above, or on top; distinct from 上る and 上げる.

exampleSentence.japanese: かいだんを上がります。
exampleSentence.reading: かいだんをあがります。
exampleSentence.english: I go up the stairs.

上がる|あがる.notes: Common motion/change verb for going up or rising; keeps 上がる distinct from 上る and 上げる.

exampleSentence.japanese: 手を上げてください。
exampleSentence.reading: てをあげてください。
exampleSentence.english: Please raise your hand.

上げる|あげる.notes: Common verb for raising or lifting; keeps 上 -> あ in a practical classroom command.

exampleSentence.japanese: 階段を上ります。
exampleSentence.reading: かいだんをのぼります。
exampleSentence.english: I go up the stairs.

上る|のぼる.notes: Common climbing/ascending verb; useful for stairs, slopes, and route descriptions.

上下|じょうげ.meaning: up and down / top and bottom
上下|じょうげ.notes: Dictionary-backed direction/position word for up and down; useful for 下 -> げ coverage but support-only for N5.

exampleSentence.japanese: 上下に動きます。
exampleSentence.reading: じょうげにうごきます。
exampleSentence.english: It moves up and down.

exampleSentence.japanese: 友だちは日本語が上手です。
exampleSentence.reading: ともだちはにほんごがじょうずです。
exampleSentence.english: My friend is good at Japanese.

上手|じょうず.notes: Core beginner adjective for being good at something; 手 is higher-level support and 上 -> じょう anchors the N5 placement.

exampleSentence.japanese: 寒いので上着を着ます。
exampleSentence.reading: さむいのでうわぎをきます。
exampleSentence.english: I wear a jacket because it is cold.

上着|うわぎ.notes: Common clothing word for jacket or outerwear; useful support for 上 -> うわ with 着 visibly labeled as higher-level.

exampleSentence.japanese: 毎朝パンを食べます。
exampleSentence.reading: まいあさぱんをたべます。
exampleSentence.english: I eat bread every morning.

食べる|たべる.notes: Core verb for eating; the example keeps 食べる in a daily breakfast context.

exampleSentence.japanese: 日本の食べ物が好きです。
exampleSentence.reading: にほんのたべものがすきです。
exampleSentence.english: I like Japanese food.

食べ物|たべもの.notes: Core beginner noun for food; 物 is higher-level kanji support and the N5 focus remains 食 -> た.

exampleSentence.japanese: 家で食事をします。
exampleSentence.reading: いえでしょくじをします。
exampleSentence.english: I have a meal at home.

食事|しょくじ.notes: Core meal word; 事 is higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 食 -> しょく.

新聞|しんぶん.notes: Core JLPT word for newspaper; 新 is higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 聞 -> ぶん.

exampleSentence.japanese: 父は新聞を読みます。
exampleSentence.reading: ちちはしんぶんをよみます。
exampleSentence.english: My father reads the newspaper.

exampleSentence.japanese: あの人は先生です。
exampleSentence.reading: あのひとはせんせいです。
exampleSentence.english: That person is a teacher.

人|ひと.notes: Core noun for person; this word-card reading is ひと, separate from counters and suffix readings like にん and じん.

exampleSentence.japanese: 水を一杯ください。
exampleSentence.reading: みずをいっぱいください。
exampleSentence.english: Please give me a glass of water.

水|みず.notes: Core noun for water; this word-card reading is みず, separate from weekday and compound readings.

exampleSentence.japanese: 水曜日に学校へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: すいようびにがっこうへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: I go to school on Wednesday.

水曜日|すいようび.notes: Core weekday word for Wednesday; 曜 is higher-level support and the N5 focus covers 水 -> すい and 日 -> び.

生える|はえる.notes: Dictionary-backed support verb for growing or sprouting; useful for 生 -> はえる coverage but support-only for N5.

exampleSentence.japanese: 草が生えています。
exampleSentence.reading: くさがはえています。
exampleSentence.english: Grass is growing.

生け花|いけばな.notes: Common Japanese culture word; retained because it gives real 生 -> いける usage in a concrete learner-friendly topic, with 花 visibly labeled as JLPT N4 kanji.

exampleSentence.japanese: 母は生け花を習っています。
exampleSentence.reading: はははいけばなをならっています。
exampleSentence.english: My mother studies flower arrangement.

生ビール|なまびーる.notes: Common adult restaurant word for draft beer; useful support for 生 -> なま in a real mixed kanji-katakana word, but support-only for N5.

exampleSentence.japanese: 父は店で生ビールを飲みました。
exampleSentence.reading: ちちはみせでなまびーるをのみました。
exampleSentence.english: My father drank draft beer at the restaurant.

生まれる|うまれる.notes: Useful for hearing the うまれる reading of 生 in a very common word.

exampleSentence.japanese: 赤ちゃんが春に生まれます。
exampleSentence.reading: あかちゃんがはるにうまれます。
exampleSentence.english: The baby will be born in spring.

生地|きじ.notes: Common fabric or cloth-material sense; 生地 is ambiguous, so this card teaches fabric/material and supports 生 -> き and 地 -> じ with 地 visibly labeled as higher-level.

exampleSentence.japanese: この生地はやわらかいです。
exampleSentence.reading: このきじはやわらかいです。
exampleSentence.english: This fabric is soft.

生徒|せいと.notes: Common N5 school word; 徒 is a higher-level kanji and must stay labeled on the N5 card.

exampleSentence.japanese: 生徒が学校にいます。
exampleSentence.reading: せいとががっこうにいます。
exampleSentence.english: The student is at school.

exampleSentence.japanese: 学校は町の西にあります。
exampleSentence.reading: がっこうはまちのにしにあります。
exampleSentence.english: The school is in the west part of town.

西|にし.notes: Core direction word for west; this word-card reading is にし, separate from compound readings.

exampleSentence.japanese: 西口から出ます。
exampleSentence.reading: にしぐちからでます。
exampleSentence.english: I leave through the west exit.

西口|にしぐち.notes: Practical station/signage word for west exit; 口 is higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 西 -> にし.

西洋|せいよう.notes: Common culture and geography word; retained because it gives useful 西 -> せい usage with 洋 visibly labeled as JLPT N4 kanji.

exampleSentence.japanese: 西洋の音楽も好きです。
exampleSentence.reading: せいようのおんがくもすきです。
exampleSentence.english: I also like Western music.

exampleSentence.japanese: 先に行ってください。
exampleSentence.reading: さきにいってください。
exampleSentence.english: Please go ahead.

先|さき.notes: Core word for ahead, before, or the front; the example teaches the beginner-useful 先に pattern.

exampleSentence.japanese: 先月、新しい車を買いました。
exampleSentence.reading: せんげつ、あたらしいくるまをかいました。
exampleSentence.english: Last month I bought a new car.

先月|せんげつ.notes: Core time word for last month; useful for past events and schedules.

exampleSentence.japanese: 先週、学校へ行きました。
exampleSentence.reading: せんしゅう、がっこうへいきました。
exampleSentence.english: I went to school last week.

先週|せんしゅう.notes: Core beginner time word for last week; 週 is higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 先 -> せん.

exampleSentence.japanese: 先生は学校にいます。
exampleSentence.reading: せんせいはがっこうにいます。
exampleSentence.english: The teacher is at school.

先生|せんせい.notes: Core classroom word for teacher; useful for school and polite address contexts.

千|せん.notes: Core number word for one thousand; this card teaches 千 as せん for standalone number use.

exampleSentence.japanese: 千まで数えます。
exampleSentence.reading: せんまでかぞえます。
exampleSentence.english: I count up to one thousand.

exampleSentence.japanese: この本は千円です。
exampleSentence.reading: このほんはせんえんです。
exampleSentence.english: This book costs 1,000 yen.

千円|せんえん.notes: Core price expression for 1,000 yen; useful for shopping examples.

exampleSentence.japanese: 川の水がきれいです。
exampleSentence.reading: かわのみずがきれいです。
exampleSentence.english: The river water is clean.

川|かわ.notes: Core nature noun for river; this word-card reading is かわ, separate from the suffix reading がわ.

前|まえ.notes: Core word for front or before; the example uses the practical 駅の前 location pattern.

exampleSentence.japanese: 駅の前で待ちます。
exampleSentence.reading: えきのまえでまちます。
exampleSentence.english: I will wait in front of the station.

足下|あしもと.notes: Common watch-your-step word; retained because 足下 is a valid あしもと spelling that gives real 下 -> もと usage, while notes make clear this is not just coverage padding.

exampleSentence.japanese: 足下に気をつけてください。
exampleSentence.reading: あしもとにきをつけてください。
exampleSentence.english: Please watch your step.

exampleSentence.japanese: このかばんは大きいです。
exampleSentence.reading: このかばんはおおきいです。
exampleSentence.english: This bag is big.

大きい|おおきい.notes: Core adjective for big or large; the example uses a simple physical-size context.

exampleSentence.japanese: 大学で日本語を勉強します。
exampleSentence.reading: だいがくでにほんごをべんきょうします。
exampleSentence.english: I study Japanese at a university.

大学|だいがく.notes: Core school word for university; useful for education and study contexts.

大好き|だいすき.notes: Common N5 na-adjective; 好 is a higher-level kanji and must stay labeled on the N5 card.

exampleSentence.japanese: 日本語が大好きです。
exampleSentence.reading: にほんごがだいすきです。
exampleSentence.english: I love Japanese.

大使館|たいしかん.notes: Core place/travel word for embassy; 使 and 館 are higher-level support, and generated pitch remains visibly labeled.

exampleSentence.japanese: 大使館は駅の近くです。
exampleSentence.reading: たいしかんはえきのちかくです。
exampleSentence.english: The embassy is near the station.

大人|おとな.notes: Common whole-word reading for adult; do not split 大人 into fake per-kanji readings.

exampleSentence.japanese: 大人はここで待ちます。
exampleSentence.reading: おとなはここでまちます。
exampleSentence.english: Adults wait here.

大勢|おおぜい.notes: Common N5 quantity word for many people; 勢 is a higher-level support kanji and must stay visibly labeled.

exampleSentence.japanese: 人が大勢います。
exampleSentence.reading: ひとがおおぜいいます。
exampleSentence.english: There are many people.

大変|たいへん.notes: Very common N5 adjective/adverb; retained because it is essential learner vocabulary and gives real 大 -> たい usage, with 変 visibly labeled as JLPT N3 kanji.

exampleSentence.japanese: この宿題は大変です。
exampleSentence.reading: このしゅくだいはたいへんです。
exampleSentence.english: This homework is tough.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今日は私の誕生日です。
exampleSentence.reading: きょうはわたしのたんじょうびです。
exampleSentence.english: Today is my birthday.

誕生日|たんじょうび.notes: Core birthday word; 誕 is higher-level support and the N5 focus covers 生 -> じょう and 日 -> び.

男|おとこ.notes: Can sound blunt when used alone. 男の人 is safer for man; 男の子 means boy.

exampleSentence.japanese: あの男の人は先生です。
exampleSentence.reading: あのおとこのひとはせんせいです。
exampleSentence.english: That man is a teacher.

男の子|おとこのこ.notes: Common beginner word for boy; fixed の expression that belongs as a word card, not arbitrary phrase padding.

exampleSentence.japanese: 公園に男の子がいます。
exampleSentence.reading: こうえんにおとこのこがいます。
exampleSentence.english: There is a boy in the park.

exampleSentence.japanese: あの男の人は先生です。
exampleSentence.reading: あのおとこのひとはせんせいです。
exampleSentence.english: That man is a teacher.

男の人|おとこのひと.notes: Common beginner word for man; dictionary-backed fixed の expression, not arbitrary phrase padding.

男子|だんし.notes: Common in school, sports, and category labels for boys or male students; 男の子 is safer for everyday 'boy', so this card is recognition/support for 男 -> だん.

exampleSentence.japanese: 男子は先に入ります。
exampleSentence.reading: だんしはさきにはいります。
exampleSentence.english: The boys go in first.

地下|ちか.notes: Common location word; retained because it gives useful 下 -> か usage in practical underground/basement contexts, with 地 visibly labeled as JLPT N4 kanji.

exampleSentence.japanese: 地下の店で昼ご飯を食べました。
exampleSentence.reading: ちかのみせでひるごはんをたべました。
exampleSentence.english: I ate lunch at the basement shop.

exampleSentence.japanese: かばんの中にペンがあります。
exampleSentence.reading: かばんのなかにペンがあります。
exampleSentence.english: There is a pen in the bag.

中|なか.notes: Core location word for inside or middle; the example uses the beginner-useful かばんの中 pattern.

中国|ちゅうごく.notes: Reading-coverage support word for the common 中 -> ちゅう pattern; also a common country name for China.

exampleSentence.japanese: 中国へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: ちゅうごくへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: I am going to China.

exampleSentence.japanese: そのえんぴつは長いです。
exampleSentence.reading: そのえんぴつはながいです。
exampleSentence.english: That pencil is long.

長い|ながい.notes: Core adjective for long distance, length, or time; the example uses a simple physical-length context.

天の川|あまのがわ.notes: Reading-coverage support word for the 天 -> あま pattern; fixed lexical item for the Milky Way, not arbitrary phrase padding.

exampleSentence.japanese: 夜、天の川を見ます。
exampleSentence.reading: よる、あまのがわをみます。
exampleSentence.english: I see the Milky Way at night.

exampleSentence.japanese: 晩ご飯に天ぷらを食べました。
exampleSentence.reading: ばんごはんにてんぷらをたべました。
exampleSentence.english: I ate tempura for dinner.

天ぷら|てんぷら.notes: Common food word for tempura; this mixed form uses 天 for てん while ぷら stays kana.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今日は天気がいいです。
exampleSentence.reading: きょうはてんきがいいです。
exampleSentence.english: The weather is nice today.

天気|てんき.notes: Core weather word; useful for daily small talk and planning.

exampleSentence.japanese: 部屋の電気をつけます。
exampleSentence.reading: へやのでんきをつけます。
exampleSentence.english: I turn on the room light.

電気|でんき.notes: Core everyday word for electricity or lights; useful for room and household contexts.

exampleSentence.japanese: 電車で学校へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: でんしゃでがっこうへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: I go to school by train.

電車|でんしゃ.notes: Core transportation word for train; useful for commuting and school examples.

exampleSentence.japanese: 友だちに電話をかけます。
exampleSentence.reading: ともだちにでんわをかけます。
exampleSentence.english: I call my friend on the phone.

電話|でんわ.notes: Core communication word for phone or phone call; useful with 電話をかける.

土|つち.notes: Core concrete noun for soil or earth; this word-card reading is つち, separate from weekday compounds like 土曜日.

exampleSentence.japanese: 手に土がつきました。
exampleSentence.reading: てにつちがつきました。
exampleSentence.english: My hands got dirt on them.

土地|とち.notes: Common land or place word; useful support for 土 -> と with 地 visibly labeled as higher-level.

exampleSentence.japanese: この土地は大きいです。
exampleSentence.reading: このとちはおおきいです。
exampleSentence.english: This piece of land is large.

exampleSentence.japanese: 土曜日に友だちと会います。
exampleSentence.reading: どようびにともだちとあいます。
exampleSentence.english: I meet a friend on Saturday.

土曜日|どようび.notes: Core weekday word for Saturday; 曜 is higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 土 -> ど.

exampleSentence.japanese: 駅の東に大きい公園があります。
exampleSentence.reading: えきのひがしにおおきいこうえんがあります。
exampleSentence.english: There is a big park east of the station.

東|ひがし.notes: Core direction word for east; this word-card reading is ひがし, separate from compound readings.

exampleSentence.japanese: 東京へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: とうきょうへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: I go to Tokyo.

東京|とうきょう.notes: Core place name for Tokyo; 京 is higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 東 -> とう.

exampleSentence.japanese: 東口で待ちます。
exampleSentence.reading: ひがしぐちでまちます。
exampleSentence.english: I will wait at the east exit.

東口|ひがしぐち.notes: Practical station/signage word for east exit; 口 is higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 東 -> ひがし.

読みます|よみます.notes: Polite form of 読む; useful for hearing the よみ reading directly, but it is reviewed as a conjugated support form rather than a separate JMdict headword.

exampleSentence.japanese: 毎晩、本を読みます。
exampleSentence.reading: まいばん、ほんをよみます。
exampleSentence.english: I read a book every night.

exampleSentence.japanese: 毎晩、本を読みます。
exampleSentence.reading: まいばん、ほんをよみます。
exampleSentence.english: I read a book every evening.

読む|よむ.notes: Core verb for reading; the example keeps 読む in a practical book-reading context.

exampleSentence.japanese: 南の国へ行きたいです。
exampleSentence.reading: みなみのくにへいきたいです。
exampleSentence.english: I want to go to a southern country.

南|みなみ.notes: Core direction word for south; this word-card reading is みなみ, separate from compound readings.

exampleSentence.japanese: 駅の南口で会います。
exampleSentence.reading: えきのみなみぐちであいます。
exampleSentence.english: I will meet at the station's south exit.

南口|みなみぐち.notes: Useful station/location word for south exit; 口 is a higher-level support kanji and must stay visibly labeled.

二|に.notes: Core standalone number form for two; this card teaches the に reading for number and number-sequence use.

exampleSentence.japanese: 数字を二から五まで言います。
exampleSentence.reading: すうじをにからごまでいいます。
exampleSentence.english: I say the numbers from two to five.

exampleSentence.japanese: コーヒーを二つお願いします。
exampleSentence.reading: こーひーをふたつおねがいします。
exampleSentence.english: Two coffees, please.

二つ|ふたつ.notes: Core native counter form for two things; useful for beginner quantity requests.

二時|にじ.notes: Common N5 time expression that covers 二 as に and 時 as じ.

exampleSentence.japanese: 二時に駅で会いましょう。
exampleSentence.reading: にじにえきであいましょう。
exampleSentence.english: Let's meet at the station at two o'clock.

二十歳|はたち.notes: Common age word with a whole-word reading; 歳 is a higher-level kanji and the card must not be split into false per-kanji readings.

exampleSentence.japanese: この人は二十歳です。
exampleSentence.reading: このひとははたちです。
exampleSentence.english: This person is twenty years old.

二十日|はつか.notes: Common date and duration word with a whole-word reading; do not split it into false per-kanji readings.

exampleSentence.japanese: 二十日に帰ります。
exampleSentence.reading: はつかにかえります。
exampleSentence.english: I will go home on the twentieth.

二人|ふたり.notes: Core people-count word for two people; useful for pairs and small-group examples. Learn 二人 as the fixed reading ふたり.

exampleSentence.japanese: 友だちと二人で映画を見ます。
exampleSentence.reading: ともだちとふたりでえいがをみます。
exampleSentence.english: My friend and I will watch a movie together.

二日|ふつか.notes: Common date/duration word with a whole-word reading; do not split it into false per-kanji readings.

exampleSentence.japanese: 二日に学校へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: ふつかにがっこうへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: I go to school on the second.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今日はいい日です。
exampleSentence.reading: きょうはいいひです。
exampleSentence.english: Today is a good day.

日|ひ.notes: Core word for day or sun; this card teaches 日 as ひ, separate from date and weekday readings.

exampleSentence.japanese: 日本へ行きたいです。
exampleSentence.reading: にほんへいきたいです。
exampleSentence.english: I want to go to Japan.

日本|にほん.notes: Core country name for Japan; useful for travel, identity, and language examples.

exampleSentence.japanese: 日本語を毎日勉強します。
exampleSentence.reading: にほんごをまいにちべんきょうします。
exampleSentence.english: I study Japanese every day.

日本語|にほんご.notes: Core language word for Japanese; useful for study and classroom contexts.

exampleSentence.japanese: この人は日本人です。
exampleSentence.reading: このひとはにほんじんです。
exampleSentence.english: This person is Japanese.

日本人|にほんじん.notes: Core word for a Japanese person; useful for nationality and identity examples.

日曜日|にちようび.notes: Core N5 weekday word; covers the contextual 日 -> にち reading in 日曜日 while the final 日 is read び in the same word.

exampleSentence.japanese: 日曜日は家で休みます。
exampleSentence.reading: にちようびはいえでやすみます。
exampleSentence.english: I rest at home on Sunday.

exampleSentence.japanese: 教室に入る前にノックします。
exampleSentence.reading: きょうしつにはいるまえにのっくします。
exampleSentence.english: I knock before entering the classroom.

入る|はいる.notes: Core intransitive verb for entering or going in; contrast with 入れる for putting something in.

exampleSentence.japanese: かばんに本を入れます。
exampleSentence.reading: かばんにほんをいれます。
exampleSentence.english: I put the book into my bag.

入れる|いれる.notes: Common transitive verb for putting something in; keeps 入れる distinct from 入る.

入学|にゅうがく.notes: Common school word for entering school; 学 is higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 入 -> にゅう.

exampleSentence.japanese: 四月に小学校へ入学します。
exampleSentence.reading: しがつにしょうがっこうへにゅうがくします。
exampleSentence.english: I will enter elementary school in April.

exampleSentence.japanese: 入口はあちらです。
exampleSentence.reading: いりぐちはあちらです。
exampleSentence.english: The entrance is over there.

入口|いりぐち.notes: Core navigation word for entrance; 口 is higher-level support and the N5 focus remains 入 -> いり.

年|とし.notes: Core word for year or age; this word-card reading is とし, separate from counters and compounds like ねん.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今年はいい年です。
exampleSentence.reading: ことしはいいとしです。
exampleSentence.english: This year is a good year.

白|しろ.notes: Core color noun for white; this card teaches 白 as しろ and complements the adjective 白い.

exampleSentence.japanese: 白が好きです。
exampleSentence.reading: しろがすきです。
exampleSentence.english: I like white.

exampleSentence.japanese: 白い猫がいます。
exampleSentence.reading: しろいねこがいます。
exampleSentence.english: There is a white cat.

白い|しろい.notes: Core i-adjective for white; learner-friendly color word and 白 reading support.

白紙|はくし.notes: Common paper and school word; retained because it gives useful 白 -> はく usage in a concrete blank-sheet context, with 紙 visibly labeled as JLPT N4 kanji.

exampleSentence.japanese: 白紙に名前を書いてください。
exampleSentence.reading: はくしになまえをかいてください。
exampleSentence.english: Please write your name on the blank sheet.

白髪|しらが.notes: Common concrete word for gray or white hair; retained because it gives real 白 -> しら usage with 髪 visibly labeled as JLPT N2 kanji.

exampleSentence.japanese: 祖父の白髪が増えました。
exampleSentence.reading: そふのしらががふえました。
exampleSentence.english: My grandfather has more gray hair now.

白米|はくまい.notes: Common food word; retained because it gives useful 白 -> はく usage in a real rice vocabulary item, with 米 visibly labeled as JLPT N3 kanji.

exampleSentence.japanese: 白米を少し食べます。
exampleSentence.reading: はくまいをすこしたべます。
exampleSentence.english: I eat a little white rice.

八|はち.notes: Core standalone number form for eight; useful for number sequences and counting contexts.

exampleSentence.japanese: 数字を八から十まで言います。
exampleSentence.reading: すうじをはちからじゅうまでいいます。
exampleSentence.english: I say the numbers from eight to ten.

exampleSentence.japanese: みかんを八つもらいました。
exampleSentence.reading: みかんをやっつもらいました。
exampleSentence.english: I received eight mandarins.

八つ|やっつ.notes: Core counter form for eight things; this card teaches the やっつ reading for general counting.

exampleSentence.japanese: 学校は八時に始まります。
exampleSentence.reading: がっこうははちじにはじまります。
exampleSentence.english: School starts at eight o'clock.

八時|はちじ.notes: Core time expression for eight o'clock; useful for schedules and daily routines.

八日|ようか.notes: Common date and duration word with a whole-word date reading; kept for 八 -> よう support without pretending it is a regular 八 plus 日 compound.

exampleSentence.japanese: 八日に学校へ行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: ようかにがっこうへいきます。
exampleSentence.english: I go to school on the eighth.

八百屋|やおや.notes: Common N5 shop word with a lexicalized whole-word reading; 屋 is a higher-level kanji and this must not be split into false per-kanji coverage.

exampleSentence.japanese: 八百屋で野菜を買います。
exampleSentence.reading: やおやでやさいをかいます。
exampleSentence.english: I buy vegetables at the greengrocer.

半|はん.notes: Core word for half and half-past time expressions; this card teaches 半 as はん.

exampleSentence.japanese: 今は三時半です。
exampleSentence.reading: いまはさんじはんです。
exampleSentence.english: It is half past three now.

exampleSentence.japanese: ケーキを半分食べました。
exampleSentence.reading: けーきをはんぶんたべました。
exampleSentence.english: I ate half of the cake.

半分|はんぶん.notes: Core quantity word for half; useful for food and sharing contexts.

彼女|かのじょ.notes: Very common pronoun and girlfriend word; retained because it gives real 女 -> じょ usage in an essential learner-facing word, with 彼 visibly labeled as JLPT N3 kanji.

exampleSentence.japanese: 彼女は日本人です。
exampleSentence.reading: かのじょはにほんじんです。
exampleSentence.english: She is Japanese.

飛行機|ひこうき.notes: Core transportation word for airplane; 飛 and 機 are higher-level support, and generated pitch remains visibly labeled.

exampleSentence.japanese: 飛行機で行きます。
exampleSentence.reading: ひこうきでいきます。
exampleSentence.english: I will go by airplane.

百|ひゃく.notes: Core number word for one hundred; this card teaches 百 as ひゃく for standalone number use.

exampleSentence.japanese: 百まで数えます。
exampleSentence.reading: ひゃくまでかぞえます。
exampleSentence.english: I count up to one hundred.

exampleSentence.japanese: このペンは百円です。
exampleSentence.reading: このぺんはひゃくえんです。
exampleSentence.english: This pen is 100 yen.

百円|ひゃくえん.notes: Core price expression for 100 yen; useful for shopping examples.

父|ちち.notes: Use 父 for your own father when speaking to others. Use お父さん for someone else's father or when addressing your father.

exampleSentence.japanese: 父は会社で働いています。
exampleSentence.reading: ちちはかいしゃではたらいています。
exampleSentence.english: My father works at a company.

exampleSentence.japanese: 日本語が少し分かります。
exampleSentence.reading: にほんごがすこしわかります。
exampleSentence.english: I understand a little Japanese.

分かる|わかる.notes: High-utility verb for understanding; the 分 reading is word-specific and separate from minute/part senses.

分かれる|わかれる.notes: Common concrete verb for splitting or branching; useful support for 分 -> わかれる, but support-only for N5.

exampleSentence.japanese: 道が二つに分かれています。
exampleSentence.reading: みちがふたつにわかれています。
exampleSentence.english: The road splits in two.

分ける|わける.notes: Common concrete verb for dividing or sharing; useful support for 分 -> わける, but support-only for N5.

exampleSentence.japanese: ケーキを二つに分けます。
exampleSentence.reading: けーきをふたつにわけます。
exampleSentence.english: I divide the cake into two pieces.

exampleSentence.japanese: 先生に日本語の読み方を聞きます。
exampleSentence.reading: せんせいににほんごのよみかたをききます。
exampleSentence.english: I ask the teacher how to read it in Japanese.

聞く|きく.notes: Core verb for hearing, listening, or asking; the example uses the practical ask sense.

母|はは.notes: Humble/plain way to refer to your own mother; use お母さん for someone else's mother.

exampleSentence.japanese: 母は毎朝早く起きます。
exampleSentence.reading: はははまいあさはやくおきます。
exampleSentence.english: My mother gets up early every morning.

母語|ぼご.notes: Dictionary-backed language word for native language; useful for learner identity and 母 -> ぼ support, but support-only rather than core beginner family vocabulary.

exampleSentence.japanese: 私の母語は英語です。
exampleSentence.reading: わたしのぼごはえいごです。
exampleSentence.english: My native language is English.

帽子|ぼうし.notes: Core clothing word for hat or cap; useful support for 子 -> し with 帽 visibly labeled as higher-level.
